question: What means, taken together, are said to suffice in the context addressed to the fair-faced one?
premises: An address is made to the fair-faced one.
That means is also what has been heard.
inference: Mere knowledge, together with what has been heard, is the means indicated here.
uncertainties: The fruit of these means is not stated in this verse.
plain_english: By this mere knowledge, and by what has been heard, O fair-faced one.
